description:
## Question

What is the reuse policy, independent of the mechanism?
- Are failing results cached and replayed, or always re-run? (Bazel re-runs failures. Meta's buck2 stance is to cache "usually only passing tests".)
- Which labels opt a target out of caching (quokka's set, Bazel's `external` / `no-cache`)? Is caching on by default or opt-in per target?
- How does a user force a re-run (a flag on `tk test`, a label, a per-invocation config)?
- What else, beyond inputs, must invalidate a result: timeout changes, test args and filters, a new version of the tool itself?

comments.text:
Resolution (grilled 2026-09-25). Glossary terms (recorded result, result key, reuse policy) added to CONTEXT.md in commit https://github.com/firefly-engineering/turnkey/commit/fee7c9f0e308.

Reuse policy, independent of the mechanism:
1. Only passes are recorded results. Fail, timeout and fatal always re-run; nothing but passes is ever read or published. The same rule applies locally and remotely.
2. Default on: once a test rule supports caching, all its targets are cached. How a rule becomes safe to cache belongs to turnkey-w55.8.
3. One per-target opt-out label, `no-test-cache`: always run, never record. The reason goes in a comment next to it. We rejected quokka's reason-named label set and Bazel's `external`. A separate 'don't publish remotely' label is deferred to the shared-cache handover question.
4. Forced re-run: `tk --no-test-cache test <patterns>`. It is a tk-level flag before the subcommand, like --no-sync. It skips reads but still records fresh passes. This deliberately differs from Bazel, where --cache_test_results=no also stops publishing. There is no env-var or config equivalent in v1.
5. Result key = everything the test process can see (inputs, argv incl. --test-arg and .turnkey/local.toml args, declared env incl. --env, timeout, cwd, platform), plus the buck2 version and the caching tool version as an explicit salt. Filters are argv, so a filtered run gets its own key. The timeout goes in the key on every tier, to avoid Bazel's #30576 local/remote drift.
6. When correctness and hit rate conflict, a wrong hit is never acceptable: when in doubt, miss. Undeclared ambient reads (PATH, HOME) are keyed, scrubbed or pinned, or the test is opted out; they are never trusted. This is the tie-breaker for later tickets.
7. Only under tk: a plain `buck2 test` neither reads nor records results, because tk is the entry point that guarantees fresh cells.
8. The policy stays outside the result key, so changing it never splits recorded results.
Retries: not applicable. The OSS buck2 test runner has no retries, so there is no 'flaky pass' to decide about.

title: When may a recorded test result be reused?
